the presence of a shock or crisis, as well as the associated vulnerabilities, is a necessary condition for the implementation of a ‘bouncing back strategy’, whereas anticipatory capacities are a necessary condition for implementing a ‘bouncing forward strategy’.

anticipatory capacities, in combination with the perceived vulnerability of local governments, are the main factors that determine their organizational response strategies in the face and in the wake of shocks and crises.

local governments should not only focus on bouncing back strategies, but should also develop anticipatory capacities to enable bouncing forward strategies in order to better cope with shocks and crises.
